title: Derived completeness of limits of elementwise nilpotent torsion complexes
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal, and let $(L_n)_{n\geq1}$ be an inverse system in $D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose that for every $f\in I$ and every $n$ there exists an integer $e\geq1$ such that the endomorphism $f^e:L_n\to L_n$ is zero in $D(A)$. Then $R\varprojlim_nL_n$ [def-weil-derived-limit] is derived complete with respect to $I$ [def-weil-point-derived-complete-module-complex]: for every $f\in I$ the derived limit of the constant system on this object with transitions multiplication by $f$ is zero.

source.place: Tag 091W, lemma-naive-derived-completion, specialization with the tensor factor K=A[0]

proof.text: Products in the category of $A$-modules are exact: kernels are coordinatewise and a tuple in a product of surjective targets lifts by choosing a preimage in each coordinate. Apply clauses (1) and (2) of [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence] to this abelian category. Thus all countable products needed below exist in $D(A)$, and all towers in question have derived limits, unique up to isomorphism.

Fix $n$ and $f\in I$, and choose $e\geq1$ with $f^e\operatorname{id}_{L_n}=0$. Put $P=\prod_{j\geq1}L_n$ and define $s:P\to P$ by $\mathrm{pr}_j s=f\mathrm{pr}_{j+1}$. The product universal property [def-weil-category-product] gives, by induction on $r$, $\mathrm{pr}_j s^r=f^r\mathrm{pr}_{j+r}$: the induction step composes with $s$ and uses $\mathrm{pr}_{j+r}s=f\mathrm{pr}_{j+r+1}$. At $r=e$ every projection is zero, hence $s^e=0$. The finite geometric sum $t=1+s+\cdots+s^{e-1}$ satisfies $(1-s)t=t(1-s)=1-s^e=1$. Thus the middle arrow in the Roos triangle [def-weil-derived-limit] for any $T(L_n,f)$ is invertible.

Write this triangle as $T\xrightarrow{p}P\xrightarrow{1-s}P\xrightarrow{\delta}T[1]$. Consecutive composites vanish by [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact]; invertibility of $1-s$ gives $p=0$ and $\delta=0$. Rotate backwards to $P[-1]\xrightarrow{-\delta[-1]}T\xrightarrow{p}P\to P$ using [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Exactness of $\operatorname{Hom}(T,-)$ at $T$, again [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact], factors $\operatorname{id}_T$ through the zero map $-\delta[-1]$, so $\operatorname{id}_T=0$. An object with zero identity is a zero object: every map out of it or into it factors through its identity and is therefore zero. Thus every $T(L_n,f)$ is zero. Since $f$ was arbitrary, [def-weil-point-derived-complete-module-complex] says that each $L_n$ is derived $I$-complete.

Put $Q=\prod_{n\geq1}L_n$. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-module-derived-complete-products-triangles] makes $Q$ derived $I$-complete. Any derived limit $H$ of the given tower has a distinguished Roos triangle $H\to Q\xrightarrow{1-u}Q\to H[1]$ by [def-weil-derived-limit], where $\mathrm{pr}_n u$ is the given transition $L_{n+1}\to L_n$ composed with $\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}$. Clause (2) of the same closure lemma applies to its two complete vertices $Q,Q$, giving derived completeness of $H$. By [def-weil-point-derived-complete-module-complex] this says precisely that $T(H,f)=0$ for every $f\in I$. No common exponent across the indices $n$ is needed.
